subtopics.title: From a Single Pulse to a Travelling Wave

questions.question: A transverse wave is best described as:
options: A single hump running along a rope
A continuous train of transverse pulses — a repeated disturbance transferring energy
A disturbance in which particles move parallel to the travel

questions.question: In a transverse pulse, the particles of the medium move:
options: At right angles — perpendicular — to the direction the pulse travels
In the same direction the pulse travels

questions.question: A clothes peg clipped to the rope, after a pulse has passed, is found:
options: At the far end of the rope
Back where it started — the medium stays; only energy is passed along

questions.question: Equal pulses on opposite sides of the rest line overlap completely. At that instant, and just after, the rope:
options: Is flat forever — the pulses destroyed each other
Is momentarily flat, then both pulses continue on unchanged
Shows a double-height hump that persists
Reflects both pulses back the way they came

questions.question: A crest rises 8 cm above the rest line and the trough sinks 8 cm below it. The amplitude is:
options: 8 cm — 0,08 m — measured from the rest line, never crest to trough

questions.question: Wavelength is defined as the distance between:
options: A crest and the nearest trough
The rest line and a crest
The two ends of the rope
Two successive points in phase — such as crest to the very next crest

questions.question: Two points on a wave are in phase when they:
options: Have the same displacement and move in the same direction — a whole number of wavelengths apart
Have the same displacement, whatever their directions
Are exactly half a wavelength apart
Are both on the rest line at any moment

questions.question: A point at a crest and a point at the very next trough are:
options: In phase, half a wavelength apart
Out of phase, half a wavelength apart — an odd number of half wavelengths
Out of phase, one full wavelength apart

subtopics.title: Period, Frequency and the Wave Equation

questions.question: The period of a wave is the:
options: Number of waves passing a point per second
Time taken for one complete wave to pass a fixed point, in seconds

questions.question: Ten complete waves pass a cork in 4 s. The frequency is:
options: 2,5 Hz — ten waves divided by four seconds

questions.question: A ripple tank vibrator runs at 25 Hz and the ripples are 2 cm apart. The wave speed is:
options: 0,5 m·s⁻¹ — v = fλ = 25 × 0,02 after converting to metres

questions.question: Harbour swells travel at 2,4 m·s⁻¹ with a period of 0,8 s. Their wavelength is:
Before substituting into v = fλ, a wavelength of 2 cm must be written as:
A wave has a period of 0,2 s. Its frequency is:
options: 5 Hz — frequency is one divided by the period

questions.question: The repeating interval on a displacement-versus-time graph of one particle is the:
options: Period — the time axis means you are watching one particle oscillate

questions.question: The source shaking faster on the same medium makes the wave:
options: Keep its speed while the wavelength shortens — the medium sets the speed

questions.question: During the stadium wave, each supporter:
options: Runs one seat sideways each ripple
Moves straight up and down, back into the same seat

questions.question: The stadium wave is called transverse because:
options: The people move at right angles to the direction the wave travels
It carries people around the stadium

questions.question: What actually travels around the ground in the stadium wave?
options: The energy of standing up, handed from block to block

subtopics.title: Measuring a Wave with a Skipping Rope

questions.question: On the shaken skipping rope, the amplitude is measured from:
options: The relaxed flat line of the rope up to the top of a hump
The top of a hump down to the bottom of a dip
One hump-top to the next hump-top
The fence pole to your hand

questions.question: If you double the rhythm of your shaking, the humps on the rope become:
options: Half as long — twice as many humps share the same rope

questions.question: Five complete humps pass your friend's shoe every second. Each hump takes:
options: 0,2 s — the period is one divided by the frequency

questions.question: Shaking the rope harder — higher humps at the same rhythm — mainly increases the wave's:
options: Energy, shown as a larger amplitude

questions.question: The wave equation v = fλ says that speed equals:
options: The number of waves per second multiplied by the length of each wave
The length of each wave divided by the number per second
The number of waves per second divided by their length

questions.question: A vibrator taps water 25 times a second and each ripple is 2 cm long. The ripples advance at:
options: 0,5 metres per second — 25 × 0,02, after converting to metres

questions.question: Swells at 2,4 m·s⁻¹ have a period of 0,8 s. Working backwards, each swell is:
options: 1,92 m long — 1 ÷ 0,8 gives 1,25 per second, and 2,4 ÷ 1,25 shares out the distance

questions.question: Before measuring anything off a wave graph, you should first:
options: Read the horizontal axis label — distance means wavelength, time means period
